warning_texts: This profile is single-vendor: every context in the run, including this red team, is claude-opus-5, so my agreement with earlier PASS results is not independent review; only the deterministic layer (machine gates, frozen check_plan, control lock, release surface gate) holds, and no GPT or cross-vend

Writes over raw_data and the frozen machinery were closed by permissions.deny for edit tools only, not for the shell, so a modified raw file would have been caught after the fact by the control lock rather than prevented; the lock digest is not among my inputs and I did not verify it myself.

All five LLM auditor results (gate0_semantic, gate_clean_auditor, gate_metrics_auditor, gate_claims_auditor, gate_release_auditor) have 'driver e2e' summaries, a fixed created_at of 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z and evidence notes containing no calculation, and gate_claims_auditor says it recomputed from ana

All four worker results are the same template: each reports refund rate 0.473684 'recomputed independently' (including worker_clean, which computes no rate), lists only its src/ script as artifact and has no disclosures field, so the absence of reported deviations says nothing about whether a stage

The frozen check_plan has no rule comparing a claim's population or period text with its metric or the spec, and no rule reads report prose beyond caveat presence and country codes; the population mislabel passed all fifteen upstream steps through exactly that gap.

gate_release_document's claims_rendered and caveats_rendered sit under accepted_unproven because the plan proof crashed with FileNotFoundError, so neither rule was ever shown to fire on a broken release, while gate0_machine's plan_proven check reports 0 accepted unproven.

The spec period ends 2025-03-30 while questions.md and the exclusion reason speak of the reported quarter and the metrics registry names the period 2025-Q1-delivered; calendar Q1 ends 2025-03-31, and although no row is dated 2025-03-31 so net revenue is 35,741.52 either way, a later export would sil

The refund-rate numerator counts a customer as refunded on any refund_amount > 0, a reading fixed only by the check_plan's flag_identity rule and not by the spec; 21 of the 33 refunded rows are partial refunds, and if refunded meant fully refunded the rate would be 0.210526 (12/57) instead of the pu

The refund_rate_basis ruling (paying_customers) gives 0.473684 against 0.189655 (33/174) on order rows, a factor of 2.498 in line with the risk register; all 57 customers have positive net revenue, so how 'paying' is read does not move the number.

The net_of_refunds ruling subtracts each refund in the quarter of its order date, and the export has no refund date, so the 4,493.50 of refunds may include refunds issued after the quarter; this assumption moves net revenue 35,741.52 and all three country figures.

The Europe/Warsaw timezone ruling cannot be checked against the data because order_date is a plain date with no time, and the report never states it; if the export's dates were UTC, the boundary rows O00008, O00082, O00198 (2025-01-01) and O00064 (2025-03-30) are the ones that could move in or out o

The R04 row accounting (201 raw, 174 kept, 26 not delivered, 1 outside the period, 27 excluded) is correct against raw but exists only in analysis/answers/R04.json, and R05 (customer lifetime value) is excused in the check plan; neither the exclusions nor the fact that R05 is unanswered reaches a re

The dashboard cards have no population field, so a dashboard reader learns the population only from the caveat strings; those caveats do say delivered orders, which makes the dashboard correct but leaves the report's population line as the only population statement a reader sees.

The four worker carries are near-identical boilerplate (same pitfalls and hints, grain 'one row per delivered order' even for worker_release), all list raw_data/orders.csv under do_not_reread although it is not an output of the previous stage, and define the population as status=delivered without th

metrics/calculated_metrics.json stores gross 40235.02 under 'numerator' of net_revenue, a non-ratio metric; it is not rendered anywhere, but a consumer reading the registry generically could show gross next to the net headline.

gate_metrics_machine does not recompute excluded_order_rows or excluded_outside_period directly (its unchecked.json says so) and relies on component sums; I recomputed both from raw as 27 and 1, matching the registry.

I could not establish that src/release/build_release.py contains no business-number literals: release_surface_gate.json records rendered numbers only, not the generator scan, and src/ is outside my inputs.

The handoff has no drift_since_review, which does not prove the stage code's assumptions hold on this export; retry history, stale inputs and runner state were not given to me and I did not check them, so the human should read them in audit_runner.py report.
